instruction: Select one or two distinct upgrade quotes for the packing floor. Each quote is independently installable at the start of the year, and added hourly capacity is additive. The approved limits are 12000 cents of total purchase cost and 3000 cents of total first-year depreciation, inclusive. Compute each quote’s full-year straight-line depreciation as purchase cost less residual value divided by useful life, applying the division to the difference. Each difference divides exactly by its positive life. Maximize added packs per hour, then minimize total purchase cost, then choose the binary-lexicographically smallest citation string. The citation string consists of the selected quote IDs sorted ascending and joined with a comma. IDs are unique single uppercase letters. At least one quote is feasible. All inputs are nonnull. Return the single winning row with quote_ids, added_packs_hour, spend_cents, annual_dep_cents in that column order. Submit a SQLite SELECT that produces the requested output using the supplied tables.

rows: Wide feeder adds 48 packs per hour.

instruction: Select exactly two distinct relief offers for one queue. Each offer can be taken once. The single row of surge_plan gives the spending cap in cents and the forecast number of calls beyond regular capacity in the early and late blocks. Offers list additional calls they can handle in each block and their flat fee in cents. Capacities add within a block. Spare capacity cannot transfer between blocks. Among pairs whose total fee is at most the cap, maximize the total forecast calls covered across both blocks. Break ties by lower total fee, then by the lexicographically smallest ordered pair of offer codes. Codes are unique lowercase ASCII strings, all values are nonnull, and at least one pair is affordable. Return one row with first_offer, second_offer, covered_calls, total_cents, placing the smaller code first. Submit a SQLite SELECT that produces the requested output using the supplied tables.

Select exactly two distinct proposed repairs for one shutdown. Each proposal card authorizes work in the loop named on it. Both repairs must use the same loop. One crew performs them sequentially. Charge the loop's setup minutes once and add both repairs' work minutes. The total may equal, but cannot exceed, the loop's window minutes. Each loop has one window record. Maximize the sum of the repairs' estimated monthly water savings in liters. Break ties by fewer total shutdown minutes, then by the lexicographically smallest pair of card IDs after sorting the two IDs ascending. Card IDs are unique. Return one row with first_card, second_card, saved_liters, shutdown_minutes, window_id. Cite the actual two proposal cards and the window record used. All fields are non-null and at least one pair is feasible. Submit a SQLite SELECT that produces the requested output using the supplied tables.

rows: East isolation includes a ten-minute drain and refill.

Repack the east drain valve stem.
Replace the east branch union gasket.
Replace the west header bleed seal.
Renew the west strainer cover gasket.

instruction: Report the lower weighted median glaze concentration in mg/L. Each batch has two replicate measurements and a positive weight equal to the number of jars it represents. A NULL measurement means the replicate is missing. Exclude the entire batch if either replicate is missing. For each remaining replicate, a below-limit flag of 1 means its recorded value is a detection limit in mg/L. Substitute half that limit. A flag of 0 means use the recorded concentration directly. Average the two resulting concentrations to get the batch concentration, then assign that average the full jar weight. Combine weights at equal concentrations. Return the smallest concentration whose cumulative weight in ascending concentration order reaches at least half the retained weight. An exact halfway tie therefore selects the lower concentration. Return one row with the single column median_mg_l. Submit a SQLite SELECT that produces the requested output using the supplied tables.
